Outbound1,1641,16257%83% 43736% 15458% 11537% 6138% 8232% 59More
What owners report
Owners say Outbound airbeds go soft overnight or after a handful of uses, and some top seams split near the grooves. They like the built-in pump and using the bed at home for guests, and owners who topped up after the first day or two say the bed then stayed firm.
What it means for you
Holding air is 83% complaints on this brand, so it is your first fix. Tell owners about the early top-up and strengthen the top seams.
What to do
  • Tier 1: Print on the box and listing that a new bed stretches and needs a top-up after the first and second day, since owners who did this say it stayed firm all night.
  • Tier 2: Reinforce the seams around the grooves on the top surface of Outbound airbeds, and pack a patch made for flocked tops.

Owners praise the wide padded seat and value of the recliner, and some bought it at Canadian Tire to replace an old zero gravity chair. They report a bent frame on first use, recline locks that pop out, an XL with a short leg rest and plastic arms.

Owners compare the leg rest length to the XL label. Put true leg rest length and the tallest sitter it suits on the listing.

Changemakers: what is new, at a glance12 products, 7 approachesThree of the seven new approaches we found are worth following now. Most of them shift the trade between comfort and packed size. The three are MEC's own double pad, the reclining Lounger Cot, and posture-first chairs. Follow means learn from it now. Watch means track it. Niche means a small market or a carried brand.
Approach A
Accept bulk, keep foam
Thick foam beds that cannot go soft overnight. Owners who comment on these beds often say comfort is worth the bulk.
Approach B
Foam comfort, packed with air
Self-inflating foam and air pads that roll smaller than foam alone.
Approach C
Add height
Raised beds and high seats that make getting up easy.
Approach D
Change the cot
Cots that recline, stack, or fit big bodies.
Approach E
Bag as bedding
Blankets, quilts, and sheet systems in place of a sleeping bag.
Approach F
The chair as the comfort product
Chairs built around posture, recline, and fit.
Approach G
The vehicle as the bed
Mattresses cut to the car.
Approach BFollow
MEC Reactor 6.5 and 10 Double
C$269.95 and C$439.95 at MEC, own brand
What it changes
MEC sells its own double self-inflating pad, and it draws a lot of reviews. The two sizes have about 200 reviews between them, all written on mec.ca.
What owners tell us
Several owners say it ended their airbed troubles. Their repeat complaints are the stuff sack, valves with no spare parts, and days to self-inflate when new.
“Sadly, my hips have told me that the days of the Thermorest / Reactor 4 sleeping pads are well past me. Not so with the Reactor 10 which provided several nights of comfortable sleeps, even for someone who sleeps on his hips!” E12171
“First time we used it took 3 days for the pad to fully self inflate. Guessing that this was because it was tightly rolled for a long period. Deflated and re-rolled. Next day it fully inflated in about an hour.” E12203
What it means for you
Woods already sells a 4 in double (Comfort Max Double, 19 reviews). MEC's 200 reviews show what to get right on the Woods double: the sack, the valves, and the fill time.
Approach AWatch
HEST Foamy and Dually
US$ price, we didn't find it sold in Canada
What it changes
A 4 in all-foam camping mattress that owners use to replace airbeds, cots, and rooftop-tent foam.
What owners tell us
Owners with back pain and rooftop tents love it. The costs are a rising price and the effort of rolling it tight enough for the straps.
“I recently swapped out my air mattress in my RTT for the Dually Long and I'll never go back. It has completely changed my level of comfort at camp, and I am finally able to get quality sleep.” E11943
“I bought my dually wide in 2021 when this company was first starting out. I paid 499, even back then that was a steep price and now it’s 629 in 2025.” E11947
What it means for you
HEST shows that owners will carry a big roll for a bed that stays firm all night. We didn't find it sold in Canada.
Approach BWatch
Exped MegaMat Duo
C$529.95 at MEC
What it changes
The MegaMat Duo combines open-cell foam with air chambers. Owners compare other pads to it.
What owners tell us
Owners say it sleeps like a home bed. Altitude Sports owners call the Medium an oversized single. They also wait hours for it to self-inflate.
“We even use it as an air mattress as a spare bed at home. Rolled up, it's definitely huge. The little pump that comes with it is slick and connects positively to the mattress so it doesn't fall our when filling.” E11558
“I dunked it underwater and lo-and-behold, at least half a dozen areas at the base of the mat where the material had thinned(?) and was leaking air. I tried desperately to patch the thinned areas of material but to no luck.” E2988
What it means for you
Owners often compare other pads to it for comfort, and it costs far more than your pads.
Approach BWatch
NEMO Roamer Double
C$499.95 at MEC
What it changes
The Roamer uses less foam and more air than the MegaMat, so it rolls to about half the size.
What owners tell us
Canoe campers like the smaller roll. Couples feel the other sleeper move. They also miss having tabs to join a second pad.
“Nemo Roamer for canoe camping. It’s just as comfortable as the Exped, but it rolls down to half the size of the Exped and can fit in to a large dry bag.” E10655
“Only down fall is you can feel a lot of movement from the other person. Also the double wide does not have the tabs to join another mattress.” E11698
What it means for you
It shows how the comfort tier can answer packed size.
Approach CWatch
Zempire Monstabed
C$499.95, MEC exclusive
What it changes
The Monstabed bonds a foam mat to an air base. At 42 cm high, it sleeps like a raised bed.
What owners tell us
Owners like the firm base and the adjustable top. Owners call it bulky and heavy.
“The base gives a firmer surface than the cots I tested (no sagging, good for stomach sleeping) and you can adjust the top part to be as soft as you need. And it makes no noise.” E5308
“Folding / rolling the pad gets rid of most of the air - the pump Flattens it - as much as it is going to get flattened: easily fits back inside the carry case.) Pro: Extremely comfortable; Con: Bulky & heavy....” E5686
What it means for you
It gives height without a cot frame. We found only a few Canadian reviews of it.
Approach CWatch
Helinox Cot Max and Cot One Convertible
C$539.99 to C$689.99 at Altitude Sports
What it changes
Clip-in legs give two heights from one frame.
What owners tell us
Owners call it luxurious and easy to set up. Some mention the price. Some report sag and a leg fitting that broke.
“Glad I got the larger (max) size of this cot. It really is luxury. Very easy to set up and super light. Don't think it'll be taken hiking with me but it's great for car camping.” E11703
“One complaint is the support straps do not become taught enough causing the bed to sag some in the middle. Don't know how they get a rating for 300lbs. It may support 300lbs but sleeping would be like in a hammock.” E8991
What it means for you
The two-height idea could work at a fraction of this price.
Approach DFollow
Cabela's Lounger Cot
C$349.99 at basspro.ca
What it changes
A cot with a reclining back and foot rest that owners use like an adjustable bed.
What owners tell us
Owners with reflux and bad backs love the incline. Owners report failures at the twist knobs and plastic lock parts.
“The best part is you can incline your head and your feet. It's just like having an adjustable bed. So comfy. It's on the expensive side but you absolutely are getting the value out of the increased cost.” E12296
“The large plastic nobs make it very hard to change sleep positions. Always hitting my elbows. The nobs should be below not above the pipe. The top should have more padding. I have to use a sleeping pad with it.” E12290
What it means for you
A cot that doubles as a lounger meets the need for comfort and the need to get up easily in one product.
Approach DNiche
Disc-O-Bed XL
C$354.99 at basspro.ca, C$379.99 at Costco
What it changes
A cot that stacks into bunks or splits into two beds.
What owners tell us
Owners value the build and the bunk layout. They warn that it weighs about 70 lb.
“I have a daughter that uses a wheelchair, and we'd use it as a portable change table when visiting family out of town. Very well built. And well worth the money. Do a few stretches before moving them around!!!” E8852
“This thing is very heavy coming in at 70lbs so may not be for everyone. Home Depot and Canadian Tire are selling this for $530. So nice discount on an already lower price from Costco.” E8845
What it means for you
You already carry it, so you can sell or bundle it as it is.
Approach EWatch
Rumpl blankets, and Zenbivy sheet-and-quilt beds
C$96.94 on sale at MEC (Rumpl)
What it changes
Blankets and quilts that replace the sleeping bag, often with a fitted sheet on the pad.
What owners tell us
Owners bring blankets and sheets from home. One says Walmart sells a Rumpl lookalike for $25.
“Walmart has an Ozark Trail Rumpl knockoff for $25. We are car camping this summer and we are taking sheets, and those.” E7966
“We have a queen rumpl blanket. It's good in summer but it's not enough for fall night time temps.” E5498
What it means for you
It matches the cottage-duvet habit you described for your rectangular bags.
Approach FFollow
Strongback Elite and Guru
Sold through dealers we found online
What it changes
A lumbar curve built into the frame, with separate seat and back panels.
What owners tell us
One owner with back pain says it is the first chair they can sit in for hours. Weight and price are the costs.
“I have a bad lower back and this is the first chair I have found that I can actually sit in for an extended period of time.” E11725
“The design which has separate back and seat parts, allows your body to "fit" into the chair, finding the most comfortable and supportive position.” E11738
What it means for you
Back-pain buyers pay for posture. Woods Lakeview Lumbar already sells lumbar support at C$79.99. The opening is a higher seat and armrests to push up from.
Approach FWatch
NEMO Stargaze and Moonlite
C$140.19 to C$229.95 at MEC
What it changes
Seats that hang and recline with body weight.
What owners tell us
Owners call it relaxing and worth the upgrade. People with limited mobility find it hard to get out of. Moonlite owners report a short seat.
“We bought a set of these after buying and trying a cheaper brand. The difference is upgrades worth paying for!” E11605
“Got mine at MEC on sale and man it is something you have to try before judging it. It is difficult for people who have difficulties with mobility but it's so comfortable and relaxing.” E9961
What it means for you
Its comfort makes getting up harder. Any reclining design will need to solve that.
Approach GNiche
Luno vehicle mattress
C$699.95 at MEC
What it changes
An air and foam mattress cut to the car's cargo floor, with a fitted sheet.
What owners tell us
Owners like the bed-like fit. Some balk at the price.
“The Luno mattress is custom fit to the car, so there is no dead space, and they have a fitted sheet, so it's a much more "Bed-like" sleep.” E7881
“they are currently charging $330 for this product for a Subaru Crosstrek. $270 for other vehicles they can tell me it’s a premium product all they want but there’s a limit to what i’m willing to pay for “premium” inflatable” E10932
What it means for you
Owners do sleep in their vehicles. Luno serves that use at a premium price, for a small market.

The direct answers
  • Leak mentions barely move with construction. Leaks come up in 25% to 31% of reviews in every group, from Coleman's coils to Woods' layered beams. Leaks come up about as often whatever the label says.
  • One-star shares do move. They follow the pump and the brand. Coleman's coil beds with a separate pump draw 15% one-star reviews. Woods Tritech beds draw 19% to 27%, and the ToughGuard bed with the most reviews draws 20%. Coil-beam beds, mostly Outbound, draw 32%. The two Outbound beds with a built-in manual pump draw 56%.
  • Outbound already sells coil beds. Nine Outbound and Woods beds carry a coil-beam label today. As a group they draw 32% one-star reviews, among the highest we read. On its own, a return to coil is unlikely to lift Outbound's ratings.
  • Material and pump already set Woods apart from Outbound. Most Woods double-high beds use Tritech layered beams or a ToughGuard shell, and some have rechargeable or overnight top-up pumps. Outbound beds use PVC and flocked tops with built-in or manual pumps. In their praise, owners mention things they can feel, like firm edges, a size that matches the box, and a height they can sit on.
  • The construction names across the market are trademarks. Intex sells Dura-Beam (fibre-reinforced I-beams). The Tritech, ToughGuard, and AlwayzAire names on Woods beds appear to be Bestway trademarks, and Bestway signs Q&A answers for some of them. Coleman sells ComfortStrong coils. We didn't find an independent test that compares them on air loss over several nights.

Scope: every airbed on canadiantire.ca, with product pages and all reviews read on 26 Oct 2026. Leak mentions are keyword matches over all reviews. They include some "no leaks" praise, so they show how often leaks come up. They do not measure a failure rate. Groups with fewer than 150 reviews read are a light read.

What the best sellers promise
SubcategoryWhat the listings sayWhat it means for you
Cots16 of the top 30 cots on Amazon.ca, and 38 of 87 Walmart.ca cot listings, come with a cushion, mattress, or pad. 24 of the top 30 state a weight capacity in pounds.Online sellers already pair the cot and the pad as one product. Your cots sell on their own, with 250 to 300 lb ratings.
Chairs10 of the top 30 chairs on Amazon.ca are oversized, 10 are padded, 7 are heated, and 12 state a weight capacity.About a third of the top 30 chairs on Amazon.ca are oversized, and a third are padded. Heated chairs sell online too. You told us at kickoff that you dropped a heated seat over defect rates. Heated chairs make up 7 of the Amazon.ca top 30.
Airbeds12 of the top 30 on Amazon.ca have a built-in pump. Intex Dura-Beam holds 8 of the top 30 and the most-reviewed beds on Walmart.ca.The most-reviewed Intex beds online sell for about C$125 to C$130.
Sleeping pads14 of the top 30 on Amazon.ca are self-inflating, at a median of C$49.99. A memory-foam roll-up camping mattress has 2,267 reviews.Online, self-inflating pads sell well below Woods prices. One memory-foam roll-up mattress has 2,267 reviews on Amazon.ca.
Sleeping bags7 of the top 30 on Amazon.ca are cotton or flannel, and 4 are XXL or oversized. MalloMe sells at C$39.99 with 10,791 reviews.Online, roomy bags that feel like home bedding sell at low prices.

Scope: Amazon.ca best-seller lists for each subcategory, and Walmart.ca search results for each term, 26 Oct 2026. Walmart.ca lists many marketplace sellers, so its search median mixes Walmart's own range with outside sellers.

07 - Method

How we did the research

Executive summary

Quotes are copied from our evidence log by a script that matches each one against the saved copy of its page.We read more than 40,000 reviews and posts and kept 12,367 entries, from 15 kinds of public sources plus your kickoff notes. In the six largest source families, the last 50 entries we read added no new complaint theme.

How the research was done
How to read the labels in this briefQuotes link to their source, and we label each number with how it was counted.
  • Every quote has an ID, like E0071. Turn on Show sources and click it to read the original comment.
  • Pain share is negative entries plus half of mixed ones, divided by all entries on that topic.
  • Canadian means the writer or the retailer is in Canada. Reviews copied from US sites are counted as US.
  • Price windows are our estimates, because costs were not shared.
Where the evidence came from12,367 entriesThe largest share of entries comes from canadiantire.ca reviews and Reddit. Canadian voice comes mostly from canadiantire.ca, with 5,142 entries, then RedFlagDeals, Amazon.ca, Reddit, MEC, Altitude Sports, Costco.ca and Walmart.ca.

How we know we read enoughIn the six largest source families, more reading was unlikely to add new complaint themes.

Six source families were large enough to test. In each one, the last 50 entries added no new complaint theme and no new step. Steps stopped growing after about 9,000 entries.

Reviews read against entries keptCounts of what owners wrote are either reviews we read or entries we kept, and the label says which. Reviews read measure coverage. Entries kept are the evidence.

We read more than 40,000 reviews and posts in full, including 17,374 reviews on canadiantire.ca alone. Readers kept the comments that say something specific about comfort, packing, failure, or use. We logged each one as an entry with its quote, source, and coding. Those make up the 12,367 entries counted in this brief.

What still needs validation6 itemsSix claims still need checking before you act on them, including our price windows. Each rests on inference or our judgment and is marked that way.
  • Who makes the Outbound and Woods airbeds. We inferred this from trademarks and from answers signed by Bestway, BackyardFun, and Jilong.
  • The Woods canoe seat as a GCI rebadge. We inferred this from copied reviews.
  • Strongback availability in Canada. A dealer network is listed, and we did not check stock or prices.
  • Price windows. These are our estimates without costs.
  • Market calls of open or partly occupied. These are our judgment from the products we found.
  • Every pain point. Each one is a hypothesis from reviews and forums until it is checked with owners.
What this research cannot tell you4 limitsThe gaps are Canadian voice on premium products, sales data, and conversations with owners.
  • We have few Canadian reviews of premium brand products. Brand sites supply some of those reviews, such as 11% at Altitude Sports and the NEMO Tensor reviews at MEC, which are not part of the MEC own-brand count below. Owner interviews in Canada would close the gap.
  • Search trends give context. Every term rose in 2026, so we compared shares between terms.
  • We did not have your returns, warranty, or unit sales data.
  • Every pain point is a hypothesis from secondary research until it is checked with real owners.
Reference

Full lists and the detail behind the findings above.

Can you trust the star ratings?7 retailersAt four of the seven retailers we checked, most reviews were copied in from US brand and retailer sites. They are Sport Chek, Bass Pro, Walmart.ca, and Costco.ca. We counted each review once and tagged it as US when it came from a US site.

  • Sport Chek, Bass Pro, Walmart.ca, and Costco.ca show mostly US reviews copied from brand and retailer sites. A Canadian shopper reading them is mostly reading reviews first posted on US sites.
  • On canadiantire.ca, the copied reviews we found sit mainly on carried brands such as Klymit, GCI and Disc-O-Bed, where many reviews come from the brand's own site.
  • On Walmart.ca, Caddle paid a reward for 118 reviews. We tagged them and weighed them separately.
  • MEC's own products carry only reviews written on mec.ca. They give the clearest Canadian voice on a premium product.

Search setWhat moved, 2022 to 2026What it means
Self-inflating"Self inflating mattress" stays at an index of 1.5 to 2.0Few shoppers search for the format by name, so the shelf and the listing have to explain it. The shelf and the listing have to explain it.
Sleeping bags"Double sleeping bag" held at 3.5% to 3.0% of "sleeping bag"Roomy, bed-like bags do not show up as a search trend. The case for them rests on what owners say.
Height"Raised air mattress" and "high back camping chair" sit near zeroSearches for height terms like raised air mattress sit near zero. Mobility needs come through in reviews.
Cots"Camp bed" rose from 19.8 to 29.7 in 2026, "cot mattress" from 18.5 to 21.6Cot searches are climbing. So are searches for something to put on top.
New methods this round4 methodsThis round added brand-store reviews, search trends, and a check on where each review was written.
  • We used review collectors for Walmart.ca, Sport Chek, Altitude Sports, HEST, Strongback, MEC, and Cabela's. They run in a real browser and read reviews the way a shopper sees them. They did not read review feeds directly or bypass bot checks.
  • We read Google Trends for seven search sets in Canada and one in Quebec, January to October of each year from 2022 to 2026.
  • Brand-store reviews (HEST, Strongback) let us hear from the changemakers' own customers.
  • We tagged reviews we found copied from another site, so each one counts once.
